AlternateTargets: has nothing to do with it
Senses.Explanation: There is none (沒) of the dealings, involvement, connection, or bearing named by the compound (交涉): 'there is no connection' or 'it has no bearing.' The records deploy this one literal sense in two ways. First, as a plain statement of no connection. Shitou says that speech and action have no connection (言語動用沒交涉), and his disciple replies that non-speech and non-action also have no connection (非言語動用亦沒交涉). Another line says, 'before the King of Awe-Voice, no connection' (威音已前沒交涉). Second, as a dismissive verdict on a wrong answer. Blue Cliff Record comments repeatedly use 'well, no connection!' (且喜沒交涉 / 且得沒交涉), meaning that the offered account misses the recorded matter. The verdict can itself be challenged: when a monk says 'well, no connection' (且得沒交涉), Yuanwu asks, 'Where is there no connection?' (什麼處沒交涉). Intensified forms include 'utterly no connection' (全沒交涉 / 總沒交涉, 82 combined instances in the cited count), often in the line that something has utterly no bearing on one's own share (於自己分上全沒交涉). The rhetorical question 'what connection is there?' (有甚麼交涉 / 有什麼交涉, 114 occurrences of each graph form in the recorded count) states the same absence by question. The headword occurs 1,389 times in 244 allowlist texts.
Senses.Note: One meaning, 'no connection' or 'no bearing,' with two deployments: a flat statement and a dismissive verdict. Counted forms include 'well, no connection' (且得沒交涉), 37; 'utterly no connection' (全沒交涉), 21; 'altogether no connection' (總沒交涉), 82; 'completely no connection' (了沒交涉), 38; and 'a place of no connection' (沒交涉處), 14. It is corpus-wide rather than a master's signature.

Occurrences.Kwic: 瞠眼睛云。廓然無聖。且喜沒交涉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), case one, Emperor Wu asks Bodhidharma (武帝問達磨). Yuanwu's comment applies the dismissive verdict 'well, no connection!' (且喜沒交涉) to an offered reading of 'vast emptiness, nothing holy' (廓然無聖).

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云。且得沒交涉。師云。什麼處沒交涉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), in a hall address (上堂). A monk offers 'well, no connection' (且得沒交涉), and Yuanwu presses back, 'Where is there no connection?' (什麼處沒交涉).

Occurrences.Kwic: 後石頭垂語曰。言語動用沒交涉。師曰。非言語動用亦沒交涉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元). Shitou Xiqian says that speech and action have no connection (言語動用沒交涉); the disciple replies that non-speech and non-action also have no connection (非言語動用亦沒交涉).

Occurrences.Kwic: 山曰。三千里外。且喜沒交涉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), an exchange involving Yunyan Tansheng in Tanzhou (潭州雲巖曇晟). The line 'three thousand miles away' is followed by the verdict 'well, no connection' (三千里外，且喜沒交涉).

Occurrences.Kwic: 威音已前沒交涉。祖師不西來。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), in a hall address (上堂). The phrase 'before the King of Awe-Voice, no connection' (威音已前沒交涉) is a flat statement rather than an answer verdict.

Occurrences.Kwic: 於自己分上全沒交涉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of the Monk Zhuanyu Heng of Purple Bamboo Grove (紫竹林顓愚衡和尚語錄), instruction to the Chan monk Huixinzhao (示慧心照禪人). The intensified form says that it has utterly no bearing on one's own share (於自己分上全沒交涉).

Senses.Explanation: Literally, there is no nose-handle: no projecting part by which the thing can be seized or led. The phrase occurs 188 times in 88 allowlisted texts. Chan records apply it to sayings, circumstances, people, and what a listener confronts. Dahui pairs it with 'no flavor' and says there is nothing to grasp when considering the dry shit-stick or the raised saying. Another record reverses the phrase into a place of inquiry: 'investigate until there is no handle; precisely where there is no handle is good to investigate.' Wuzhun plays the compound against the positive form, saying there is some handle and entirely no handle. This recurring use for the point at which a word or encounter supplies no graspable lead is the corpus-specific extension of the animal-handle image.
Senses.Note: The varying grammatical subjects do not establish different things named by the headword; the phrase consistently predicates absence of a graspable handle. 'No flavor' is a frequent companion, not an alternate mystical sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 覺得昏怛沒巴鼻可把捉時。便是好消息也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui directly glosses the condition by saying there is nothing that can be grasped.

Occurrences.Kwic: 但於話頭上看。看來看去。覺得沒巴鼻沒滋味心頭悶時。正好著力。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui applies 'no handle, no flavor' to looking at the raised saying.

Occurrences.Kwic: 參禪參到無巴鼻，沒巴鼻處正好參。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A verse makes the handleless point itself the place to investigate.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖師巴鼻，衲僧巴鼻。有些巴鼻，全沒巴鼻。因甚如此？公驗分明。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wuzhun contrasts having some handle with having none at all.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘has no flavor’ or ‘tasteless.’ The corpus predicates it of sayings, inquiry, food imagery, and an interlocutor’s appraisal. A verse on Nanquan’s ‘ordinary mind is the way’ calls it ‘cold and bland, entirely without flavor,’ yet says that each raising is new. Dahui repeatedly places a person at the point where bringing up the matter feels tasteless, like a lump of hot iron or biting an iron spike, and explicitly says that this is then a good place and must not be abandoned. Later records likewise join ‘nowhere to set a hand,’ ‘without flavor,’ and ‘the road of mind cut off’; one calls the sect’s tea and rice iron-nail rice and wood-chip soup, ‘without flavor’ however long chewed, then calls that tasteless place a good state. The phrase can remain an ordinary adverse verdict: after a master answers with ‘one melon seed, two shell-halves,’ a monk says ‘no flavor,’ and the master hisses. Zen usage bends the sensory predicate by applying it repeatedly to words and sustained inquiry, and by recording masters who name the very tasteless point positively. This entry reports those descriptions without recategorizing them.
Senses.Note: One adjectival predicate across food, sayings, and inquiry: all are described as lacking flavor. These are different subjects but not different lexical things or word classes, so item 8 does not require a split. Positive and negative appraisals are text-drawn contrasts, not separate readings supplied by this entry.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南泉平常心是道。頌云。勸君不用苦勞神。喚作平常轉不親。冷淡全然沒滋味。一回舉起一回新。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui's verse applies the phrase to Nanquan's saying and juxtaposes tastelessness with renewed raising.

Occurrences.Kwic: 提撕來提撕去。沒滋味。心頭恰如頓一團熱鐵相似。那時便是好處不得放捨。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui calls the tasteless, hot-iron point a good place and says not to relinquish it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 心未明了。覺得迷悶沒滋味。如咬鐵橛相似。時正好著力。第一不得放捨。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A second distinct Dahui formulation compares the experience to biting an iron spike.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一時不得放過。直捱到無下手處，沒滋味處，心死路絕處，連絕也不知。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later record enumerates no place to set a hand, tastelessness, and the mind-road cut off.

Occurrences.Kwic: 宗門茶飯如同鐵釘飯、木楂羹，嚼來嚼去沒滋味。若到者沒滋味處，正是好境界，不生退志，終成大器。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Food imagery and the explicit positive appraisal occur together.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：「和尚起期，還是為人？為己？」師云：「一箇瓜子兩瓣殼。」進云：「沒滋味。」師噓一聲。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The phrase functions as an interlocutor's plain adverse appraisal of an answer.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, to have no tracks or traces: "leave no trace" or "be without a trace." The phrase occurs 356 times in 119 allowlisted texts. Its dominant Chan deployment is Decheng the Boatman's injunction to Jiashan: "where you hide the body, leave no trace; where no trace remains, do not hide the body" (藏身處沒蹤跡，沒蹤跡處莫藏身). That two-part wording accounts for 151 occurrences of "where no trace remains" (沒蹤跡處) and is also turned into paired interview questions. Elsewhere the phrase stands as a short predicate: a person "going away" is described as "silent and still, leaving no trace" (寂寥寥沒蹤跡), in contrast with a person "coming back" who is "bright and distinct, with news" (明歷歷有消息). Another verse pairs "no trace" (沒蹤跡) with "news cut off" (斷消息). These are the direct contrasts recorded in the corpus.
Senses.Note: Productive forms confirm the ordinary track-and-trace grammar: "absolutely no trace to seek" (了無蹤跡可尋; 11 occurrences of 了無蹤跡), and "leave no trace" (不留蹤跡; 10 occurrences). The direct question "what is the place where the hidden body leaves no trace?" (如何是藏身處沒蹤跡) occurs in five texts. The paired answers preserved here—"the moon sets, and the pool has no reflection" (月落潭無影) and "clouds arise, and the mountain has clothing" (雲生山有衣)—show how later records continue to ask each half separately. Across these forms the headword remains a trace predicate.

Occurrences.Kwic: 他後直須藏身處沒蹤跡。沒蹤跡處莫藏身。吾在藥山三十年。祇明此事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Quoted injunction by Decheng the Boatman to Jiashan: where you hide the body, leave no trace; where no trace remains, do not hide the body. The quotation itself says that Decheng understood only this matter during thirty years at Yaoshan.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問法眼。承教有言。從無住本立一切法。如何是無住本。眼云。形興未質名起未名。頌曰。沒蹤跡。斷消息。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A verse on Fayan's answer pairs no trace with news cut off. The headword-bearing words occur in the later verse, so no master attribution is imposed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂僧問。如何是向去底人。師云。寂寥寥沒蹤跡。進云。如何是却來底人。師云。明歷歷有消息。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Direct contrast: the person going away is silent and still, leaving no trace; the person coming back is bright and distinct, with news.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「如何是藏身處沒蹤跡？」師云：「月落潭無影。」「如何是沒蹤跡處莫藏身？」師云：「雲生山有衣。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The two halves of the Boatman saying are asked separately: the answers are the moon setting with no reflection in the pool, and clouds arising so the mountain has clothing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 小參云。好兄弟。行行沒蹤跡。石馬著金鞭。住住不凝停。木人敲玉戶。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Paired lines: moving, moving, leave no trace—the stone horse wears a golden whip; staying, staying, do not remain fixed—the wooden person knocks on the jade door.

RelatedTerms: where no trace remains, do not hide the body (沒蹤跡處莫藏身)
